content: Nitrofurantoin, marketed as Macrobid, is specifically indicated for the treatment of acute uncomplicated urinary tract infections (acute cystitis) caused by susceptible strains of Escherichia coli or Staphylococcus saprophyticus. It is not recommended for the treatment of pyelonephritis or perinephric abscesses. To minimize the development of drug-resistant bacteria and to preserve the efficacy of Macrobid and other antibacterial agents, Macrobid should only be used to treat or prevent infections that are either confirmed or strongly suspected to be caused by susceptible bacteria. When culture and susceptibility data are available, they should guide the selection or modification of antibacterial therapy. In the absence of such data, local epidemiological trends and susceptibility patterns may inform the empiric choice of therapy. Nitrofurantoin does not achieve the broader tissue distribution seen with other agents approved for urinary tract infections. As a result, patients treated with Macrobid may be at an increased risk of persistent or recurrent bacteriuria. Urine specimens for culture and susceptibility testing should be obtained both before and after completing therapy. If bacteriuria persists or recurs following treatment with Macrobid, alternative therapeutic agents with broader tissue distribution should be considered. When deciding to use Macrobid, clinicians should weigh its lower eradication rates against the increased potential for systemic toxicity and the risk of developing antimicrobial resistance associated with the use of agents that have broader tissue distribution.
